<!-- pr-reviewer: 4ae6a9edfe63e0675c55b63c9fadbf1d960ae623 -->
**Needs changes before merge.** There's one UI bug in the vise row's jaw-opening field. The geometry, placement, commands, project key and MCP all hold.

### What looks good
- **Geometry (`crates/app/src/vise/mesh.rs`).** The side profile is extruded across the full body width, and the cap is ear-clipped.
  - The profile is simple whenever `check()` passes: the housing step sits strictly in front of the moving jaw because `length > 2*jaw_thickness + max_opening + housing_length` (`vise.rs:96`).
  - An ear that can't be found is an `Err`, never a loop.
  - Every index is bounded by `0..n` or `% m`.
  - The test pins closure (each directed edge paired once), exact outward volume and bounds for all 10 sizes at 1%, 50% and 100% opening.
- **Conservative where it matters.** Jaws are drawn the full body width. The fixed jaw runs solid from the base bottom to `jaw_height`, and the floor (z = 0) is a full base block under the stock.
- **Refusals are named.** Non-finite, zero or negative values, opening over max, body narrower than the jaws, and body too short are each refused by name. Fit refuses stock with no width or stock wider than max. A NaN pose is caught by `check_location` inside `InsertFixture`. I found no `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` in non-test code.
- **Fit-to-stock clamps the stock rather than overlapping it.**
  - The fixed jaw face is at `stock.max.y`, the moving jaw face at `stock.min.y`, and the floor at `stock.min.z`, so the faces only touch.
  - `fixture_clash` counts a sample only `PENETRATION_MM` (0.05) inside, so mated faces don't raise a false "stock sinks into fixture" warning.
  - `stock_world_aabb_for` reads the stock at its own `Location`, the same furniture frame the fixture's pose uses.
  - "Into the fixed jaw" and "wider than max" are both refused and pinned in `the_jaw_opening_follows_the_stock`.
- **Commands.**
  - `InsertVise` is a thin wrap of `InsertFixture`, so no new collision code.
  - `SetVise` is one undo unit: `UpdateModel` (local-frame facets, rev bump, facets restored on invert) plus a marker swap.
  - "Open to stock" measures along the vise's own screw axis (`quat_conjugate(pose.rot)`).
  - `TagFixture` keeps the vise params on re-bind, and `ImportFixture` drops them.
- **Project key.** The optional `vise` is skipped when `None`, with no version bump. On load `ViseDto::to_params` re-checks the law and drops nonsense with a `tracing::warn!` (`project/vise_dto.rs:61-70`).
- **The collision proof uses the real path.** `posting::verification_gate` strikes at z 19.5 and is clean at 59.5. `fixture_view::mesh_states` asserts `MeshState::Mesh`, so the verdict comes from the mesh and not a box.
- **MCP.** `add_builtin_vise` and `set_vise` build the same `InsertVise` and `SetVise`, one History step each. Unknown size, unknown dimension, opening plus from_stock together, over-max and a zero dimension are all named tool errors.
- **Process and housekeeping.** No snapshot PNGs, process files, `build.rs`, `.github`, scripts or new dependencies. Every new module carries a provenance line, and every new file is under 400 lines.

### Local results (worktree at the PR head; `upstream/main` d68d6d18 is already contained, so the trial merge was a no-op)
| What | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --no-run` | built |
| app `builtin_vise` | 6 passed |
| app `mcp_vise` | 1 passed |
| app `fixture_mesh` / `fixture_ux` / `fixture_library` | 3 / 9 / 6 passed |
| app `fixtures` / `fixture_locate` / `move_interpenetration` | 14 / 11 / 8 passed |
| app `posting` / `commands_undo` / `mcp` / `project_roundtrip` | 17 / 32 / 13 / 71 passed |
| app `fixture_route` | no such test target in camcraft-app (nothing to run) |
| ui `--lib` (CWD `crates/ui`, includes `fixture_vise_tests`, `tests::fixture_rows`) | 459 passed, 5 ignored |
| ui `fixtures` | 7 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Requested before merge
1. **With two built-in vises in one setup, the "Jaw opening" field can't be edited, and "Set opening" lands the old value** (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/fixture_rows.rs:107-109`, with `State::vise_opening` at `crates/ui/src/state.rs` near line 1417).
   - **Cause:** `vise_opening` is one `(name, mm)` slot, and each vise row resets it to its own live opening whenever the slot names another vise. With two vise rows, every frame row A resets the slot to (A, live), then row B resets it to (B, live). An edit typed into A's field is gone by the next frame, and A's "Set opening" then queues `SetVise` with the unchanged opening.
   - **Why it matters:** placing the same vise twice is ordinary (`free_name` makes "Vise 6 in (2)" for that).
   - **Reproduced:** in a local-only probe test (not pushed), I placed two 6 in vises, set the slot to `("Vise 6 in", 90.0)` and ran one frame. The slot read `("Vise 6 in (2)", 114.3)`, and clicking the first "Set opening" left the opening at 114.3.
   - **Fix:** key the draft per vise (e.g. a `HashMap<String, f64>` or `Option` per name, reset only when that vise's live opening changes or after its own Set). Pin it with a two-vise row test that edits the first vise's field across a frame and asserts the Set lands.
   - The existing `a_vise_row_sets_its_opening_and_opens_to_the_stock` test writes the slot directly with a single vise, so it can't see this.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- **Under-modelled steel.** The moving and fixed jaws are each `jaw_thickness` deep along the screw. On many real vises the moving jaw block and the fixed jaw body run deeper than the jaw plate. A tool below `jaw_height` just behind either jaw could therefore meet real steel the mesh doesn't have. Paths rarely go there, since they'd have to pass the jaw face first, and the figures are editable. Still, a separate "jaw body depth" (or a doc note that `jaw_thickness` should be the full block depth) would make the "never less than the real steel" claim hold.
- **Stale field after undo.** After an undo of `SetVise`, the row's field keeps showing the pre-undo draft until the slot resets. This goes away with the per-vise draft above.
- **Test gaps.** No test pins the drop-and-log path for an invalid `vise` key on load. The `SetVise` undo test checks rev and opening, but not that the facets return. Both behaviours look right by reading; small pins would keep them.
- **MCP skill table.** The `camcraft-mcp` skill's tool table doesn't list `add_builtin_vise` and `set_vise`. It's a process file, so this belongs to the next process-sync PR, as the body says.
- **File growth.** Files already over ~400 lines grew a little: `crates/ui/src/state.rs` (4155, +31), `crates/ui/src/egui_app/pages.rs` (+4), `crates/app/src/project/apply.rs` (+1), `project/entity.rs` (+4) and `schema.rs` (+4). Not blocking.
- The 8 in size figures were accepted by the maintainer on 2026-11-11, so I didn't re-check them.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: c2a3f87352310d96fe5a0b22068bc4ecadda92db -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** This is a delta review of c2a3f873 against the earlier review at 4ae6a9ed. That review's blocker is fixed, and so are all three of its notes.

### What looks good
- **Per-vise opening drafts.** `State::vise_opening` is now a `HashMap<String, ViseOpeningDraft { live, value }>`.
  - `vise_opening_draft` refreshes a row's draft only when that vise's live opening changes (bit compare). That covers Set, "Open to stock", undo and redo, so the stale-field-after-undo note is gone too.
  - `retire_vise_opening_drafts()` runs at the top of `fixtures_section` and drops drafts for names that are no longer built-in vises.
  - A row's own Set removes only its own draft (`state_vise.rs`).
- **Jaw body depth.** `ViseParams::jaw_body_depth` defaults to `BODY_PER_PLATE` (2) times the jaw thickness, and both jaws are drawn that deep up to jaw height.
  - It is refused by name if it is below the jaw thickness or not finite.
  - The length check now counts two jaw bodies (`vise.rs`).
  - It is exposed in the dialog (`fixture_vise_dialog.rs:59`) and over MCP: it is in `DIMS`, so it appears in the `set_vise` schema and the params view.
  - Files without the key read it as 2 times the thickness (`vise_dto.rs`, `unwrap_or(BODY_PER_PLATE * jaw_thickness)`). It is written as an optional key, so no format bump is needed.
- **Mesh shape.** The profile keeps the same 12-corner shape. `every_table_row_builds_a_closed_shell_of_its_dimensions` still checks every size at 1 %, 50 % and 100 % of max opening for: `check()`, watertightness, the expected volume (now using body depth) and bounds. So every row still fits its full max opening with the deeper bodies.
- **New pins.**
  - Undoing `SetVise` restores the old facets, and redo restores the new ones.
  - An out-of-range `vise` key on load is dropped and logged ("vise parameters dropped on load"). The fixture and its saved steel stay, and `SetVise` then refuses it as "not a built-in vise".

### Local results (PR head merged with upstream/main, clean merge)
I built with `cargo test -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --no-run` and it passed.

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| app `builtin_vise` | 9 passed |
| app `mcp_vise` | 1 passed |
| app `fixtures` | 14 passed |
| app `fixture_mesh` | 3 passed |
| app `fixture_ux` | 9 passed |
| app `fixture_library` | 6 passed |
| app `project_roundtrip` | 71 passed |
| app `commands_undo` | 32 passed |
| ui `--lib` (CWD `crates/ui`) | 460 passed, 5 ignored |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

I checked that both new pins fail without the fix. These were local mutations only, reverted and not pushed:
- I made `vise_opening_draft` behave like the old single slot (drop every other name's draft). `two_vise_rows_keep_their_own_opening_drafts` then fails at `fixture_vise_tests.rs:198` ("the first Set lands the typed opening").
- I drew the jaws at `jaw_thickness` again in `mesh.rs`. `steel_behind_a_jaw_plate_below_jaw_height_is_struck` then fails.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- **Name-keyed drafts: rename and duplicate names.**
  - Fixtures have no rename command today; `RenameOperation` is for operations only. Every fixture insert goes through `insert_fixture::free_name`, so two fixtures can't share a name. The drafts are keyed the same way every command already finds its entity (`model::find_by_name`).
  - The one case left is a reused name. If a vise is deleted while the Fixtures section isn't drawn (retire only runs there), and a new vise then takes the same name with the same live opening, the new row would show the old typed value. The draft is only what the field shows: it lands only on a visible "Set opening" click, and `SetVise` still checks it. So a stale draft can't apply silently to the wrong vise.
  - If fixture rename is ever added, retire or move the draft there, or key the drafts by entity.
- **The steel-behind pin** tests the mesh through `FixtureMesh::build(p.mesh())` with `contains` and `band_meets`. That is the fixture law's own mesh primitive, not a placed vise in a world. The posting-level conviction is still covered by the existing 6 in jaw-crossing test.
- **Untested reads.**
  - No test loads a file *without* `jaw_body_depth`; the default is clear from reading the code.
  - `mcp_vise` doesn't set `jaw_body_depth`; it comes from the shared `DIMS` list, so it's covered by construction.
  - Small pins for either would be nice in a follow-up.
- **File growth** is unchanged from the earlier note: `state.rs` grew by a few more lines, while the new draft logic lives in `state_vise.rs`.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
